draft.title: Incentives
card: An incentive is something that encourages people to make a choice. A discount or a reward is an incentive.
A disincentive is something that discourages people from making a choice. A fine or a tax is a disincentive.
Incentives and disincentives change what a choice gives or costs a person. This can change what they decide to do.
The same thing can be both. A tax on a product is a disincentive to buy it, but a discount on that product is an incentive to buy it.
draft.remember: Incentives encourage a choice. Disincentives discourage one.

a.q: A council fines people who drop litter in a park. What is the fine?
opts: A disincentive, because it discourages littering
An incentive, because it encourages littering
An incentive, because it encourages people to pay
A disincentive, because it encourages people to visit
a.why: A fine makes littering cost more, so it discourages the choice. That makes it a disincentive. It is not an incentive, because it does not encourage the choice it is aimed at.
a.clue: Does the fine make people more or less likely to litter?

b.q: Mia runs a bakery in Ballarat. She gives customers a free coffee when they buy ten pies. What is the free coffee?
opts: An incentive to buy more pies
A disincentive to buy more pies
A tax on customers who buy pies
A fine for customers who buy few pies
b.why: The free coffee is a reward that encourages customers to buy more pies, so it is an incentive. It is not a disincentive, because it does not discourage the choice to buy.
b.clue: Is the free coffee a reward or a penalty?

a.best: A disincentive, because it discourages littering

b.best: An incentive to buy more pies

problems.detail: The fourth line says 'The same thing can be both', but its example uses two different things: a tax, which is a disincentive, and a discount, which is an incentive. The example does not show one thing being both, so it confuses the idea. A fitting example is a tax on cigarettes: it is a disincentive to smoke but an incentive to quit.

check.summary: Both questions and their explanations are correct. The card's line 'The same thing can be both' is illustrated with two different things (a tax and a discount), so the example contradicts the claim and should be replaced or the line reworded.
